note: A first improvising drill that says what a question and an answer are in notes: a phrase that stops on a dot that is not ringed, then one that stops on a ringed root. The second section changes one thing, the rhythm of the answer. It moves to other keys and tempos.

exercise.title: Question and answer phrases
exercise.why: A phrase that stops on the root sounds finished and one that stops on any other note sounds unfinished, so two phrases in a row can sound like a question and its answer.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track. Under it is the neck with the notes of the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale, with the three {{1}} notes ringed.
Play a short phrase of three or four notes that stops on a dot that is not ringed: that is the question. Leave a gap, then play a second phrase that stops on a ringed {{1}}: that is the answer.
Listen for the question sounding unfinished and the answer sounding finished.

Press Play below to start the backing track again. This time the answer copies the rhythm of the question: as many notes, as long or as short, but other dots, and the last one a ringed {{1}}.
If you lose the rhythm, clap the question once, then play the answer.
Keep going until an answer comes without you planning it.
